condition_other: lower limb amputation with transected nerve endings or neuromas; phantom and residual limb pain
readout_other: Patient-reported sensation to iFU (threshold intensity); LANSS; numeric pain rating scale
direction_notes: iFU at the transected nerve ending and proximal nerve elicited sensations (including phantom limb sensations); same intensity at control tissue or intact contralateral nerve generally did not.
safety_notes: Two out of 11 study participants reported only mild and transient pain created by iFU stimulation.

exposures.label: Image-guided iFU to transected nerve ending (and proximal nerve, control tissue, contralateral nerve)

device.model: five 2.0 MHz iFU transducers with foci at 0.4, 1.3, 2.45, 2.75 and 3.0 cm

timing.protocol_description: Three to five individual 0.1-second bursts at approximately 1 Hz, intensity raised stepwise from 16 W/cm2 until a reliable sensation (two consecutive sets); maximum device output 1,032 W/cm2.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Two out of 11 study participants reported only mild and transient pain created by iFU stimulation.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: We created five 2.0 MHz iFU transducers, each with its focus at a different depth relative to the skin surface
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: we used one transducer to deliver individual single bursts of ultrasound lasting 0.1 seconds
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.ispta_w_: iFU spatial and temporal average intensity values between 16 W/cm<sup>2</sup> and 433 W/cm<sup>2</sup> that were applied to the transected nerve ending and proximal nerve elicited sensations

flags.reason: Results text mentions 11/13 participants with LANSS above 12, inconsistent with 11 participants stated elsewhere.

Range 16-433 W/cm2 is the threshold values reported in the abstract; intensities were stepped up to a device maximum of 1,032 W/cm2. Calibrated in water by hydrophone but values not stated to be free-field.
Paper says the five transducers were created by the authors, maker not named; custom_built chosen.
Sham-applied iFU is mentioned but its mechanism is not described; control tissue and contralateral nerve also stimulated actively.
Single 0.1 s burst per application, no internal gating described; recorded as continuous.
